## Appearance

Uncle Jim is a tall, somewhat stooped, and rather ungainly figure who still suggests great strength and endurance. He has big brown hands, a deeply lined, bronzed, clean-shaven face, and a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders that has grown much grayer over time. His clear, deep-set blue eyes are remarkably steady.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 34 THE SHIP O’DREAMS COMES TO HARBOR P18](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0018)_

## Personality

Captain Jim is a high-souled, simple-minded man of exceptional moral character, described as one of the finest souls. Known for his invariable cheerfulness and placid temperament, he is also a passionate worshipper of beauty. He possesses a born gift for storytelling as well as a knack for playing the fiddle, though he harbors a deep horror of dying a lingering death.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 8 MISS CORNELIA BRYANT COMES TO CALL P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P49](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0049), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P9](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0009), +3 more_

## History

As a young boy, Captain Jim ran off to sea after his friends John and Persis [Selwyn](../character/john-selwyn.md) married, sailing the world for most of his life before eventually returning home. Fifty years prior, he lost his sweetheart, [Margaret](../character/margaret.md), at sea and spent months searching the shore for her body in vain. During his seafaring years, he also brought [Dick Moore](../character/dick.md) back to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds). Five years after retiring from the sea, he welcomed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) to the neighborhood, sharing with them stories of his lighthouse life and the romantic history of their new house. Over the following months, he hosted [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), and [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) for frequent lighthouse visits, [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) dinner, and New Year's celebrations.

After comforting [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) following the loss of her infant daughter, Captain Jim shared the tragic story of [Margaret](../character/margaret.md) and entrusted [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) with her memory. He later showed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) his written life-book, which she recognized as potential material for a great literary work. When [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md) visited the harbor, Captain Jim shared his memories, entrusted Owen with his life-book, and gave him permission to turn his experiences and Margaret's memory into a novel. Though initially concerned, Captain Jim supported Gilbert's recommendation that [Dick Moore](../character/dick.md) undergo surgery in [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal). He later celebrated the publication of Owen's book with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) over tea, and passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse the following morning.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P0](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0000), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P8](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0008), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P16](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0016), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P37](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0037), [v4 CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE P2](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE P34](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0034), +41 more_

## Quotes

> "Nephew Alec. He understands it as well as I do. Well, now, I’m real glad you asked me to stay to supper. I’m proper hungry—didn’t have much of a dinner today."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P19](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0019)

> “Oh, I do, Mistress Doctor, I do,” protested Captain Jim. “Why, I live like a king gen’rally. Last night I was up to the Glen and took home two pounds of steak. I meant to have a spanking good dinner today.”
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P21](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0021)

> "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P24](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0024)

> "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032)

> "I reckon when the darkness is close to us it is a friend. But when we sorter push it away from us—divorce ourselves from it, so to speak, with lantern light—it becomes an enemy. But the fog is lifting."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 13 A GHOSTLY EVENING P17](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0017)
